bad.en: (meant: he got angry and lashed out at his friend)
bad.why: It is not 'spitting fire' at someone. It means being the first to begin, and it takes no target marked with ni.

mean: not nearly as good as one boasted
lit: not even as much as one's mouth: the deeds fall short of the words

use.how: A mocking verdict on someone who talked big and then failed: 口ほどにもないやつだ, 口ほどにもなかった. Rude if said to someone's face.

near.diff: 見かけ倒し is falling short of how something looks; 口ほどにもない is falling short of what someone boasted.

cue: Your cousin bragged all week that he was unbeatable at chess, then lost to your ten-year-old sister in five minutes. What do you say?

ctx.s: 「強[つよ]いって自慢[じまん]してたのに、{口[くち]ほどにもない}な。」
ctx.en: "You kept bragging about how strong you were, but you're nothing special."

ctx.s: 「料理[りょうり]が得意[とくい]だって言[い]ってたけど、{口[くち]ほどにもなかった}ね。」
ctx.en: "You said you were a great cook, but it wasn't all that, was it?"

ctx.s: ゲームでは無敵[むてき]だと豪語[ごうご]していた兄[あに]は、妹[いもうと]にあっさり負[ま]けた。{口[くち]ほどにもない}とはこのことだ。
ctx.en: My brother, who boasted he was unbeatable at the game, lost easily to our little sister. All talk, if ever I saw it.

ctx.s: 試合前[しあいまえ]にさんざん挑発[ちょうはつ]してきた相手[あいて]は、まったく{口[くち]ほどにもなかった}。
ctx.en: The opponent who taunted us so much before the match was nowhere near as good as his talk.

ctx.s: 大口[おおぐち]をたたいていた新人[しんじん]は、初[はじ]めての営業[えいぎょう]で一件[いっけん]も契約[けいやく]が取[と]れず、{口[くち]ほどにもなかった}。
ctx.en: The new hire who talked so big didn't land a single contract on his first sales round; he was all talk.

ctx.s: {口[くち]ほどにもない}と言[い]われたくないので、本番[ほんばん]まで必死[ひっし]に練習[れんしゅう]した。
ctx.en: I didn't want people to say I was all talk, so I practised like mad until the day of the performance.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]も自慢[じまん]しない人[ひと]だが、実力[じつりょく]は{口[くち]ほどにもない}。
bad.en: (meant: he never boasts, and his skills are poor)
bad.why: The phrase needs earlier boasting to fall short of. For someone who never boasts, just say jitsuryoku wa amari nai.

bad.s: 「下手[へた]だって言[い]ってたのに、ピアノ上手[じょうず]だね。{口[くち]ほどにもない}よ。」
bad.en: (meant: you said you were bad, but you play the piano well)
bad.why: It only means worse than claimed, and it is a put-down. For better than claimed, say omotta yori jouzu da ne.
